answer: A decaying reputation bond works like a glacier: an agent stakes value to join, and the stake melts slowly over months, so a Sybil farm must keep paying to stay present. At its nadir, when the bond is nearly gone, the agent must re-stake or lose its standing, which makes mass identity creation expensive to sustain. A falcon-style audit layer then spot-checks random accounts and demands fresh proof of work; failing a check burns the bond. The cost is continuous, not one-off, so flooding the network stops paying.
